entry: Ran src/tui/session/oauth-flows.mjs, src/standalone/session-service.mjs createSessionService().handleCall (scripted runtime factory / readStoredSession / listSessions / log), the real HTTP session transport + session-client attachSession and createSession (callId cache, client registry, remote runtime proxy) with the stub runtimes of scripts/session-transport/_shared.mjs, and src/standalone/session-proxy/transitions.mjs createTransitions. A TCP tap in front of the transport records every HTTP exchange (status line, headers in order, body). Did not run the log-summary and call-cache-metric cases (see notRecorded).
exclusions: cases 48 and 451 are listed in notRecorded with their reasons

wire taps record the HTTP exchanges in request order: `Host` header port value -> <port> and the response `Date` header value -> <date>, at those header paths; and this machine's roots (the checkout process.cwd() -> <CWD>, the OS temp dir -> <TMP>, the user home -> <HOME>, in every spelling found: as written, forward slashes, JSON-escaped, URL-encoded, each also lower-cased; text after the root, separators included, is kept) in every request/response startLine, header value, body and event-stream frame (lib/tmp-mark.mjs). The Content-Length is the one Node sent: a message that had a root replaced carries `rewrites` {label: {originalLength, count}} (a label for a spelling other than as written reads "<CWD> (JSON-escaped)"), so length(recorded body) + sum(count * (originalLength - label length)) = Content-Length. No other value is normalised
crypto.randomUUID returns 00000000-0000-4000-8000-<12-digit counter> in call order (client tokens, registration ids, server tokens, daemon session ids, call ids all come from it)
crypto.randomBytes(n) (without a callback) returns the next n values of a running byte counter modulo 256
Date.now() is 1700000000000 and performance.now() is 0 for the whole run (revisions are Date.now()*1000, queuedMs is 0) unless a case moves the virtual clock by a recorded step
process.pid is 4242 (process.kill(pid, 0) of it answers alive, as it is this process) and process.ppid is 4241; the recorded cwd is the constant "C:\\recorded\\cwd"

GLOBALS PATCHED by installDeterminism(): crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes (no-callback form), Date.now, performance.now, process.pid, process.ppid, process.kill (signal 0 of the fixed pid only). The child-process preloads (lib/determinism-preload.mjs, determinism-preload-other-process.mjs) patch crypto.randomUUID, crypto.randomBytes, Date.now and process.pid only (pid 4242, the second process 4243); they leave process.kill, performance.now and process.ppid alone

BRANCH process.pid liveness (isPidAlive / process.kill(pid, 0): src/runtime/shared/pid-liveness.mjs, ~54 files: daemon discovery in session-client, writer and process locks): the fixed pid is answered alive by the process.kill hook in the recording process; a child process preloaded with the fixed pid has no such hook, so it would judge the parent's pid dead and could steal a lock the parent held: no recorded flow has a lock held across processes (restart-prefix phases run one after the other, the lifecycle parent holds nothing while its child runs)

BRANCH process.pid equality (own-lock re-entrancy, ~33 sites such as memory-process-lock, scheduler): a recorded flow with two processes gives them different pids (4242, 4243) so they are different owners, as in production

BRANCH id collision: session ids are sess_<pid>_<n>_<Date.now()>_<randomBytes(16)>; with a fixed pid, a fixed or stepped clock and a counter for the bytes, uniqueness rests on the store's own sequence number n (nextId) and on the counters not being reset between live sessions: determinism.reset() is called only where the previous session is finished (lifecycle fresh()), and a collision would fail the save, not pass unnoticed

BRANCH ordering by time (~23 sort sites on updatedAt/createdAt): with a fixed clock timestamps tie, so a listing sorted by time falls back to insertion order; no recorded case reads a time-ordered listing of several sessions (directory listings are recorded in the OS order)

BRANCH deadlines on Date.now / performance.now (~74 performance.now sites, Date.now deadline loops such as settleTurnJournalWrites and lock timeouts): with the clock fixed they never expire inside the code under test; every wait of a recorder carries its own real-timer deadline instead, and the cases that need elapsed time move the virtual clock by a recorded step

case 299, the error texts of the failing and the unserved read ("stub failure", "session action getOutputStyle is unavailable"): Node's session call error carries the service's own message; the core answers a failed internal call with an incident id and an unserved method with capabilityUnavailable

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: Replayed over the transport harness of native/core/crates/mixdog-app-server/src/tests/wire.rs: the server behind its real WebSocket listener on a loopback port, real client connections driven as the daemon drives them, over a real session thread. Every frame each client received is compared whole and in order (session_transport.rs whole); the only normalization is wire::normalized: ids the core generates become <id:N> in order of first appearance and clock readings (*At fields, clientHostPid) become <clock>/<pid>. The recorded HTTP exchanges (wire: start lines, headers, Content-Length) are Node's HTTP/SSE framing of each call; the core's client transport is one WebSocket carrying each JSON-RPC message as one text frame (mixdog-app-server-transport websocket.rs), so the frame bodies are compared and the HTTP framing has no counterpart. Cases: 438 a_retried_start_with_the_same_op_runs_once, 507 a_reused_op_with_another_payload_fails_closed, 243 unsubscribing_never_interrupts_the_running_turn, 130 an_unknown_thread_is_refused_and_nothing_is_created, 156 the_same_op_from_another_connection_is_answered_once (the --with-the-fix case: Node patched by node-fix-call-id-once-per-session.patch accepts a call id once per session and answers the retry from another client with the first answer; replayed as two connections sending the same op id; the base-commit case records the defect, two runs of one submission, and is not replayed). Not replayed: 15 (the OAuth registry's status/complete/cancel answers are replayed from fixtures/login-status by mixdog-core-domains ai_account/tests.rs provider_sign_in_feeds_publish_the_statuses_node_answered; this case's flow starts with url null, which no core sign-in start produces: LoginState::Authorize carries a URL); 320 and 369 (Node answers a `session.configure setRoute` whose runtime then reports another session id under the addressed id; a thread's id is fixed when the core creates its actor and no method changes it, so no core answer carries another id); 465 (Node's TUI remote-runtime proxy: createSession, submit, setProgressHint, abortAsync and newSession over session.* calls with its mirrored state; the only Rust front end, mixdog-cli, is the exec command and holds no remote session projection). Replayed with declared exclusions: 82 (session_transport.rs the_thread_catalog_never_rides_a_thread_answer: Node's create, read and rename answers carry no `sessions` and its list answer does; the core's thread/read and thread/name/set answers carry no catalog; not compared: the catalog scan counts, which the core does not keep) and 299 (session_transport.rs a_failing_unserved_and_non_serializable_read_answer_as_node_does: config/getProfile, config/getOutputStyle and config/getTheme served by the stub the recording scripted, through the server over a real socket; compared: a failing read is an error answer, an unserved read is an error answer, and getTheme's answer is the recorded value; not compared: the error texts, since Node hands the stub's own message to the caller and the core never does: an internal failure answers an incident id and an unserved method is capabilityUnavailable naming it; the stub's function member cannot be a JSON value, and the date arrives as the recorded ISO text).
